We have five unitary authorities: Flintshire, County Durham, Bedford, North Lincolnshire, and Telford & Wrekin.

We need ONS data for domestic gas consumption for each unitary authority for the years 2012 and 2023. Then calculate drop (difference 2012-2023). Then identify biggest drop.

Bedford area code W06000007? We'll find.

North Lincolnshire area code W06000009? Telford & Wrekin area code W06000022? Need to confirm.

Alternatively, we can use ONS indicator dataset JSON via api, but easier to fetch each local indicator page.

We need domestic gas consumption indicator value per year.

Observation: ONS local indicator pages show "Domestic gas consumption - 2012-2024" with median value in kWh and chart year-by-year. We will extract 2012 and 2023 values.

Let's start with Flintshire.

## Interpretation

These figures are based on meter level gas consumption data. Those meters with an annual consumption less than 73,200 kWh are classified as domestic meters. This means that some small industrial and commercial consumers will be classified as domestic.

These estimates are weather-corrected. This means that the effect of differences in weather conditions between years has been removed to provide more like for like comparisons over time.

The precise time periods covered by different years of data differ:

*   Prior to 2015: October – September (same period as 2015)
*   2015: October 2014 – September 2015
*   2016: mid-July 2016 – mid-July 2017
*   2017: mid-June 2017 – mid-June 2018
*   2018: mid-May 2018 – mid-May 2019
*   2019 onwards: same pattern as 2018

Gas consumption data for 2005 to 2024 as a single table, with years stacked one above the other.

From:[Department for Energy Security and Net Zero](https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/department-for-energy-security-and-net-zero)Published:20 December 2018 Last updated: 5 May 2026 — See all updates

### Update: 5 May 2026

Tables for 2005 to 2013 were revised to correct for a processing error identified for some Local Authorities in Wales which had resulted in data being shown against incorrect Local Authorities. Total figures for Wales were not impacted.

### Update: 19 December 2025

These tables were revised to correct an error in the non-domestic gas consumption for one area in the North East. This impacts 2023 data only, which has now been corrected in this version.

## Interpretation

These figures are based on meter level gas consumption data. Those meters with an annual consumption less than 73,200 kWh are classified as domestic meters. This means that some small industrial and commercial consumers will be classified as domestic.

These estimates are weather-corrected. This means that the effect of differences in weather conditions between years has been removed to provide more like for like comparisons over time.

The precise time periods covered by different years of data differ:

*   Prior to 2015: October – September (same period as 2015)
*   2015: October 2014 – September 2015
*   2016: mid-July 2016 – mid-July 2017
*   2017: mid-June 2017 – mid-June 2018
*   2018: mid-May 2018 – mid-May 2019
*   2019 onwards: same pattern as 2018
